title: Plan and organize project work
description: Use when creating or organizing LPM backlog work: create activities (single or batch), edit fields, plan cycles/sprints and milestones (marcos), labels, owners, estimates, due dates, unassigned/unestimated/overdue queues, escalations. Not for doing or closing one activity (use lpm-deliver-activity).
doneWhen: The requested backlog structure exists, a re-read matches the plan (owners, dates, counts), and failed items are named.
authorityCeiling: Reads, creates, edits, comments, named cancels [A]; owner, estimate and date plans need a "yes"; labels, notifications, deletes [C]; no owner-only tools.
jobs: cria estas atividades no backlog do projeto <nome>
planeje o próximo sprint e feche o ciclo atual
atribua as atividades sem responsável e defina os prazos
o que está atrasado no projeto <nome>?
daily sync for project <name>: what is open and what is next
create these 12 issues in one batch
close the sprint and move the unfinished work to the next cycle
estimate the unestimated issues of project <name>
notify the assignee that the milestone date moved

notFor.when: doing or closing one activity (status done, evidence, commits)
a blocked activity or a dependency link
a new project, members or teams
an open governance thread or decision
activities that materialize an approved roadmap item
roadmap items or roadmap-level outcomes across projects

references.loadWhen: playbook daily-sync: daily sync of a project
playbook owners-dates: set owners, estimates or due dates; work a queue
playbook edit-activities: edit fields, cycle, milestone or labels of activities
playbook cancel-or-delete: cancel or delete an activity
playbook cycle-open-or-start: open or start a cycle (sprint)
playbook cycle-close: close or delete a cycle
playbook milestone: open, close, re-date or delete a milestone
playbook labels: create or merge labels
playbook escalate: escalate an activity; notify a person

codex.shortDescription: Plan LPM backlog: activities, sprints, owners and dates
codex.defaultPrompt: Use $lpm-plan-work to plan and organize the backlog of LPM project <projectId>.
